knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with permission to search `index=azure`.
• Install and configure: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (`Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Splunkbase 3110).
• Ensure `azure:monitor:activity` events are flowing (prerequisite UC: none when applicable).
• Map `azure` and field extractions per `docs/guides/aws.md`, `docs/guides/azure.md`, or `docs/guides/gcp.md` as appropriate.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Export Activity Log to Event Hub or Storage Account; configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` Azure Monitor Activity input. Alert when zero events for 60 minutes in business hours.
Expected sourcetype: `azure:monitor:activity`. Validate with:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="azure:monitor:activity" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="azure:monitor:activity"
| table _time operationName caller resourceId
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
The search scopes `azure:monitor:activity` in `index=azure` and applies `*` to surface `Azure Activity Log Baseline Ingestion and Health`. Tune time range and alert threshold to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare result counts to the vendor console (CloudTrail Event history, Azure Activity Log, GCP Logs Explorer, or service-native UI). Spot-check `_time` and actor fields. Confirm CIM acceleration only after TA field mappings are verified.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_58_alert` with appropriate severity. Dashboard: Single value (events 24h), subscription coverage table, ingestion lag..
Failure modes: (1) empty results — verify TA input and index routing; (2) duplicate events — check S3/SQS duplication; (3) missing fields — upgrade `Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (`Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Splunkbase 3110)` and review `props.conf` aliases; (4) alert fatigue — add CMDB/allow-list exclusions documented in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch for azure activity log baseline ingestion and health in your cloud audit logs so the team catches important changes early instead of finding out from auditors or customers.
